entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — September 24, 2026

Executive Summary

This week's headline is the Bot Screen launch: @NousResearch unveiled real-time screen streaming for Hermes Desktop, and Teknium followed with live visual/interactive desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent — you can now watch, and even interact with, the same machine your agent controls. Under the hood, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 shipped with 1,812 merged PRs and a new --format stream-json flag that powers the newly documented Hermes–Claude plugin pipeline, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code CLI while keeping all credentials in the CLI's own login flow. Around the ecosystem, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 hardened MCP security, rlaope open-sourced jeval and expanded oh-my-hermes, and the alpha-stage AgentProto v0.20.0 runtime arrived for multi-agent orchestration.

Releases

  • Bot Screen for Hermes Desktop — live streaming of any agent session, now official. Paired with desktop passthrough for Hermes Agent, users can watch and interact with the machine their agent is driving. Official docs are live.
  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (tagged v2026.9.21, released 21 September) — adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL for scriptable pipelines. This release underpins the new Claude plugin pipeline and broader CLI automation use cases.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 — hardens MCP with per-invocation session scoping plus identity/origin checks.
  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (Apache-2.0, released 22 September) — a new TypeScript runtime that orchestrates multiple coding agents, including Hermes, from a single scheduler. Alpha maturity: expect rough edges.

Merged PRs

  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 bundled 1,812 merged PRs. Standouts:
  • Skills auto-load — skills now load automatically.
  • Configurable MCP discovery concurrency — tune how aggressively MCP discovery runs in parallel.

Community

  • Bot Screen launch reception — euphoric and long-awaited. The launch thread drew roughly 173k views; Teknium's "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" (~20k views) captured the pent-up demand. @tonbistudio published a community walkthrough alongside the official docs.
  • OMH + Jev ecosystem — rlaope delivered the batch's strongest organic engagement (1,706 views) announcing oh-my-hermes (OMH) support for Jev-Skills and model routing, then open-sourced jeval (Jev evaluation/visualization) and shipped an updated oh-my-hermes Plus — positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for AI-native hermes-agent power users.
  • Hands-on maintenance — Teknium stayed visible: disputing a cache complaint pending a reproducible issue, celebrating a quick "fixed lol" resolution, and clarifying that a tool under discussion was built by the Nous/Hermes team, not Anthropic.
  • Broader chatter — a lukewarm take praising Opus 5.5 while questioning Claude Code's agent experience, GitHub show-and-tell prompts, and short reaction posts capped a launch-driven week.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Hermes via iMessage — the official account's practical gem: use Hermes through iMessage with whichever model you prefer (~13k views).
  • Claude plugin pipeline, explained — a deep engineering walkthrough shows Hermes driving the unmodified official Claude Code CLI over stream-json. A companion security doc confirms authentication lives entirely in the CLI's claude auth login flow — Hermes never handles or stores API keys.
  • Watching your agents work — pair Bot Screen streaming with desktop passthrough; the official docs plus the @tonbistudio walkthrough are the fastest way in.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Deep technical walkthrough of the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin pipeline: Hermes talks to the plugin, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, with conversation flowing as native stream-json while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals, and compaction. Version requirements: Hermes 0.21.4+ and a logged-in Claude Code CLI, with native 2.1.263 as the qualified version. Each request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools/skills disabled so Hermes tool inventory is what the model sees. A per-request admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request, rejecting native retry attempts locally to keep billing honest.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (tagged v2026.9.21, released 21 September 2026) adds a --format stream-json flag to the CLI that emits structured JSONL, one JSON object per line, enabling scripts and pipelines to parse Hermes output reliably. Upgrades are available via hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The same release rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency. The feature is free and built into the open-source agent.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Explains the authentication chain for the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: auth lives entirely in the official Claude Code CLI via claude auth login (browser plus pasted code); the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes, or prints credential files, and no API key is required or sent anywhere. The plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint, and cloud overrides, naming conflicting variables without printing their values. Status checks are local, with claude auth status reading the local credential store in roughly 0.3s and showing credentials confirmation. Separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR to point at a dedicated CLI-managed config.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Overview of Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub on 18 September 2026. Key changes center on MCP security: sessions are now scoped per invocation, and requests are authenticated against the correct invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives become ZIP-only with digest verification, ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected, and new vector-store connectors were added for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB, and Azure Cosmos DB plus in-memory and portable filters. The release includes breaking changes, notably deprecation of the MCP sampling callback.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Review of AgentProto, a new open-source agentic runtime written in TypeScript, released 22 September 2026 at v0.20.0 under Apache-2.0. It provides a single interface to start, message, watch, and stop any coding agent, with quality gates applied before work lands, and integrates 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode, and Mastra. Cost is limited to underlying model usage. The project is very early: single-digit GitHub stars, Tier 2 components labeled alpha scaffolding. Verdict: interesting architecture, early-adopters-only.
